issues.title: feat(calendar): the first thing in this repo that fires on a DATE, not a commit
issues.body:
## What this closes

`docs/design/WEEK_2026-08-10_PLAN.md` measured **eleven dated commitments landing inside one week, of which two had a reminder mechanism -- and both "mechanisms" were a person remembering.** The structural finding it named:

> **Every tool and CI gate in this repo fires on a COMMIT. None fires on a DATE.**

Two proven costs. `#1061` slipped 2026-08-03 -> 08-10 with nothing to catch it, and wrote its own escalation rule for a second slip -- a rule with no executor. `#1070` sat correctly diagnosed for seven days, then wrote 1,330 files into Pip's live profile and took the 2026-07-31 league board from 50 entries to 0.

**This does not fix that by itself. A file cannot ring.** It produces something a calendar app can subscribe to, and makes an undeclared date loud instead of invisible. Getting it subscribed is Pip's step, and it is on the last page of the printed sheet.

## Numbers

| | |
|---|---|
| Declared commitments parsed | **48** (24 of them the weekly cadence expanded to concrete dates) |
| Release-train events, derived from `ROADMAP.md` | 4 |
| **UNPARSED** -- a future date nothing accounts for | **24** |
| Malformed declarations | 0 |
| Total VEVENTs / VALARMs in the `.ics` | 76 / 117 |
| Print sheet | 5 A4 pages, 12.5pt body, printed |

## The declaration convention, and why this form

```
COMMITMENT: <YYYY-MM-DD> -- <what> -- owner: <who> [-- kind: <k>] [-- lead: <Nd,Nd>] [-- covers: <paths>] [-- note: <text>]
COMMITMENT: every <DAY> -- <what> -- owner: <who> -- kind: cadence -- from: <date> [-- until: <date>]
```

**One line, no file to open, no schema, no ID to allocate.** The measured failure is *not* that people record dates badly -- eleven were recorded correctly and none fired. It is that recording costs more than the moment of noticing. A convention needing a registry loses to typing the date in prose, every time, and then we are back to a scraper guessing. This one is cheap enough to write mid-sentence in a handover, an issue body or a `.gd` comment, and reads correctly to somebody who has never seen it.

**Only the DATE is positional.** House ASCII style (#744) makes ` -- ` the em-dash, so it appears constantly inside ordinary titles; a positional split would corrupt every second declaration. Everything after the date is keyword-extracted, and a chunk opening no keyword *continues whatever it follows* -- so both `A -- B` in a title and `note: X -- Y` survive.

**`owner:` is mandatory and its absence FAILS the parse.** The week's measurement found the load-bearing column was the who, not the date: an obligation another repo is publicly waiting on behaves nothing like an intention somebody expressed once. A default owner is how everything ends up assigned to Pip.

**Lead times differ by kind** and are argued in `docs/calendar/COMMITMENTS.md`: `deadline` 14/7/2/0, `expiry` 7/1/0, `review` 14/3/0, `handoff` 3/1/0, `falsifier` 1/0 (you cannot run a check early), `cadence` **day-of only** -- a reminder for a thing you already do every Thursday is the fastest way to teach yourself to swipe the whole calendar away unread.

## What it refuses to do

- **UNPARSED never vanishes.** A future date with no declaration appears in the index with file and line, *and* in the `.ics` as an `[UNPARSED]` event. There is deliberately **no silent ignore list**. A calendar that silently omits is worse than no calendar, because it looks complete.
- **`ship:hotpatch-48h` (9 issues) produces no event.** The 48 hours run from label application and GitHub records that in no field this generator can read offline. A gap named, not a date invented.
- **An imported `.ics` cannot be retracted.** The events are copies in the calendar's own database; regenerating cannot reach them. Only a *subscribed* URL is replaced wholesale on poll. The half-measure (`STATUS:CANCELLED` for a grace period) needs the generator to remember what it emitted -- state that can drift and lie. Stated as a limitation instead of engineered around.

## Determinism, which is what lets the guard live in pre-commit

**Nothing reads the clock.** The prose scan is bounded by a pinned `CALENDAR-HORIZON:` and every `DTSTAMP` derives from the event's own date, so `--check` cannot go red overnight without a human edit. A clock-reading generator would go stale by morning and train everyone to ignore it. The only networked path is `--refresh-github`, which writes a tracked snapshot.

## RED RUN RECORDED

Per Workshop 2 ruling **R6** -- *no guard counts as installed until a RED run of it has been observed and recorded.*

**Red.** Appended a `COMMITMENT:` line to `docs/ROADMAP.md`, did not regenerate:

```
$ python scripts/generate_commitment_calendar.py --check
Commitment calendar is STALE: docs/calendar/pdoom1-commitments.ics, docs/calendar/COMMITMENTS_INDEX.md
  computed: 49 declared + 4 release-train + 24 UNPARSED = 77 events; 0 malformed
  fix: python scripts/generate_commitment_calendar.py
  MISSING from the committed index: | 2026-08-18 | falsifier | RED-RUN DRILL: a commitment
    added to a source and deliberately not regenerated | pdoom1-seat | 1, 0 | `docs/ROADMAP.md:130` |
exit=1
```

**Red through the hook itself**, not just the script:

```
$ pre-commit run commitment-calendar-check --files docs/ROADMAP.md
commitment calendar (.ics + index) up to date............................Failed
- hook id: commitment-calendar-check
- exit code: 1
```

**Green.** Regenerated -> `exit=0`, 77 events. Drill line reverted and regenerated -> `exit=0`, 76 events.

The failure message **names the missing row**, so a red run is actionable without a diff tool.

## Standards compliance, checked rather than claimed

Parsed by the `icalendar` library: 76 VEVENTs. All 1,959 content lines fold to <= 75 octets (RFC 5545 3.1), CRLF throughout, ASCII-only, 76 unique UIDs.

`*.ics` is excluded from `eol=lf` in `.gitattributes` and from the three whitespace hooks -- RFC 5545 mandates CRLF and folds with a leading space, so "fixing" it produces a file a strict client rejects. Verified CRLF survives `git show HEAD:...`.

## Tests

19, weighted to the negative cases -- a generator that only proves it can emit is the class of guard this repo was burned by in #640:

- missing `owner:` rejected, not defaulted
- unknown `kind:` rejected
- recurrence without `from:` rejected
- title containing ` -- ` survives; `note:` containing ` -- ` stays in the note
- UID stable when a declaration moves down a file
- **no future date is silently dropped** -- every scanned date appears as a commitment or in the UNPARSED table
- committed outputs are not stale (the pre-commit guard, as a test)

## Files

- `scripts/generate_commitment_calendar.py` -- the generator
- `docs/calendar/COMMITMENTS.md` -- convention, horizon, cross-repo declarations, subscribe instructions (hand-edited)
- `docs/calendar/COMMITMENTS_INDEX.md`, `docs/calendar/pdoom1-commitments.ics` -- GENERATED
- `docs/calendar/github_snapshot.json` -- tracked GitHub snapshot, 72 KB
- `tools/runsheet/commitments-2026-08.html` -- the print sheet
- in-place declarations added to `docs/art/PIXELLAB_OPERATIONS.md` (spend policy expiry) and `docs/POSTMORTEM_2026-08-07_CAPTURE.md` (nine falsifiers)

## Worth a second opinion

**Whether 24 cadence events is right.** Expanding `every TH` to concrete dates makes each occurrence traceable and readable by every client, but it is 24 of the 48 declared commitments. The alternative -- an `RRULE` -- is one line in the file and invisible in the index. I chose traceability; a reasonable person picks the other.

**Whether UNPARSED belongs in the `.ics` at all.** 24 low-signal events in a calendar is exactly the flooding the inclusion bar exists to prevent. Putting them there anyway is a deliberate bet that visible noise beats invisible omission, and it is falsifiable: if Pip mutes the calendar inside a fortnight, that was the wrong call and they should move to the index only.

**Nothing here touches** `godot/scripts/ui/cold_open_sequence.gd`, the time-portal shader, `docs/design/INTRO_AND_POSTER_ART.md`, `version.txt`, `ladder_version.txt` or any tag.

issues.title: feat(intro): the cold-open arrival -- portal stitch + held frame (#1112 B1+B2)
issues.body:
Implements the #1112 ruling (2026-08-04): **B1 "Portal Stitch" approved, B2 "Held Frame" approved** (`docs/design/INTRO_AND_POSTER_ART.md`). The time_portal shader -- built FOR this sequence's #801 UPGRADE layer and shipped unused since -- is now the connective tissue of the arrival, and B2's poster is the world it resolves into. **No copy changed, no ruled timing moved, handoff and show-once gate untouched.** Zero new code paths outside the cold open.

## What a new player now sees

```
0.0s   black (unchanged hold)
0.5s   doom-red vortex grows from a point under "Doom is coming."
       (open_progress 0->1 over 1.8s, held at 42% modulate so text reads)
~5s    "But... when am I?" -- the rainy street resolves behind the swirl
       (intro_bus_strangers_help, B2's held frame, slow 1.00->1.06 push)
       and the vortex starts dying (swirl_speed + glow wind down: the
       jump is ending)
~11s   "*checks pockets*" over the held frame
~15s   the vortex collapses, handing its palette doom-red -> CRT phosphor
       green as the phone slab rises out of the street
end    "Begin >>" -> the dawn office fades up as everything else lets go
       (dawn = arrival), 0.4s of quiet, then main.tscn
```

Hold-to-skip exits instantly -- no flourish on the exit ramp. Click-to-advance fast-forwards the words without beheading the choreography (each cue rides its own Tween; cues still fire in order because beats are only entered sequentially).

## What I chose, where the ruling left latitude

- **B2 is IN, as the substrate of B1** rather than a competing intro: portal = the jump, poster = the world you landed in, dawn = arrival. The pack's own comparison table says B1 composes with the poster proposals; and the poster is `intro_bus_strangers_help` (endgame_concepts_gen2 v1, verdict **keep**, silhouette principle already reviewed into it) -- which also rhymes with the prior story beat Pip narrated in #1112 (teleport back, meet a bus). If you want pure B1, delete one BEATS cue + two consts.
- **Dawn moved to the end.** The office_wide_dawn background used to sit dimmed behind the whole sequence; per B1's spec line ("office_wide_dawn fades up only at Begin >>, so dawn = arrival") it is now invisible until the player commits.
- **Palette handoff red->green during the collapse** (the B1 spec's "palette handoff" line), implemented as tweened color uniforms, 70% of the collapse duration.

## Dials Pip might want moved (all consts in the tunable block, live-tunable in `godot/scenes/dev/portal_shader_demo.tscn`)

| Dial | Set to | Moves it how | My take |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PORTAL_ALPHA` | 0.42 | brighter = more spectacle, dimmer = more legible text | the stills show text reading fine; try 0.55 if you want the vortex louder |
| `PORTAL_OPEN_SECONDS` | 1.8 | the "pop into existence" | 1.6 (the demo default) felt abrupt against a 3.0s hold |
| `PORTAL_COLLAPSE_SECONDS` | 2.2 | how long the jump takes to die under the phone | shorter reads snappier, longer reads mournful |
| `POSTER_ALPHA_TEXT` | 0.60 | street brightness under text | below 0.5 the figures stop reading |
| `POSTER_ALPHA_PHONE` | 0.32 | street brightness under the phone slab | |
| `KENBURNS_SCALE` | 1.06 | the slow push (B2 spec value) | 1.0 disables it entirely |
| `PORTAL_SWIRL_END` / `PORTAL_GLOW_END` | 0.22 / 0.9 | how dead the vortex looks by "checks pockets" | |
| `ARRIVAL_DAWN_SECONDS` + `_HOLD` | 1.1 + 0.4 | the dawn beat before main | cut `_HOLD` to 0 if the pause annoys |

## What the deterministic capture caught (worth knowing beyond this PR)

The first capture showed the red-to-green handoff **silently not happening**: at 94% of the tween the disc was still red. Cause: the doom-red was only ever the SHADER DEFAULT -- an unset uniform is not a concrete material property, so `tween_property` had nothing to interpolate from and no-oped without an error. Fix: seed the red palette explicitly at build time (`PORTAL_RED_PALETTE`, with a comment telling the next person why "redundant" seeding is load-bearing). Re-captured; frames at t=16.2/16.8 now show the full green handoff. This is the same silent-wrongness shape the league week kept finding -- the guardrail that caught it was LOOKING at deterministic output, and the capture entry that makes that cheap is now in the registry.

## Guard rails added

`godot/tests/unit/test_cold_open_intro.gd` pins: every referenced asset ships; cues are known to the driver; the sequence still ENDS on the phone handoff (#811/ADR-0001); the LOCKED MHS string is byte-identical to the Pip-approved copy; and a static scan keeps RNG calls and direct scene changes out of the file.

**Fast gate, measured:** 1254 tests, 0 failures, 127/127 files collected (baseline on the same tree before edits: 1250 / 0 / 126).

## Assets + capture

- `intro_bus_strangers_help.webp`: 1536x1024, q82, **207 KB** (ADR-0019 rule 4 derivative; master stays in the Library). Pack delta is that one file.
- `tools/capture_cinematic.py` gains a `cold_open` registry entry (18s / 30fps / 1920x1080); unattended it plays the whole arrival and parks on the phone lock screen. Stills from the deterministic capture are in `captures/stills_cold_open/` on the dev machine (gitignored by design -- captures never enter git).

## Questions for Pip (built my best guess; answer changes are cheap)

1. **Poster in or out?** B1-pure (portal over black, no street) is one cue deletion away if the held frame reads as too much for the first 15 seconds.
2. **Demand manifest:** `tools/assets/demand/slot_picks.json` is generated ("do not hand-edit: re-run the picker"), so the poster's slot pick is declared HERE, not there. Next picker round-trip should record `cold_open held frame -> gen:endgame_concepts_gen2:intro_bus_strangers_help:v1`. Note the pack doc's intro-poster pool says 1280x854; I shipped 1536x1024 (the B2 section's own spec) -- pick one and I'll conform.
3. **Deliberately not done:** the #1112 dev-vs-alpha tool split (tuning harness classification, togglable dev keys) is a separate substantive ask and is not in this PR; same for the streaming-friendly capture runner (Pip marked it roadmap).

issues.title: #1137's event retiming made a simulated run ~38% more expensive -- is that the intended event density?
issues.body:
Split out of #1181, where this turned up while looking for something else.

## The measurement

Simulation tier, one Windows box, quiet, output discarded so disk is not a
variable, `--timeout 0`, via the runner from #1181 (PR #1192). **107 tests and
0 failures in every run** -- nothing was added, removed or skipped:

| tree | runs | mean |
|---|---|---:|
| `5731dd2e` (parent of the #1137 merge) | 434s, 412s | 423s |
| `8791ba47` (the #1137 merge itself) | 584s | 584s |
| `1ddb033d` (main, 3 days later) | 586s, 619s | 602s |

**+161s, +38%, across one merge commit.** Within-tree spread is ~5% (22s and
33s), so the delta is about seven times the noise. Everything merged since
#1137 adds nothing measurable on top (584s -> 586s).

## Why this is a balance question, not a perf question

The test count did not move. The same 107 tests simply take longer, and #1137
("retime the historical deck to one-turn-one-month, timing dial, ruled
promotions") is exactly the change that would make a simulated run do more work
per turn -- more events becoming eligible and firing inside each full-run /
replay / determinism test.

So the interesting reading is not "the sim tier got slower". It is **"a run now
contains ~38% more event processing than it did on 2026-08-06"**, which is a
statement about what a player's run feels like, and it was not measured when
#1137 landed.

## What would settle it

Count events actually fired per simulated run, pre- and post-#1137, on the same
seed. If firings are up ~38%, the runtime delta is just the deck doing what
#1137 told it to and the question becomes whether that density is the intended
one (#1125 / #1111 ruled the promotions; nobody ruled a rate). If firings are
flat and the time went somewhere else, that is a different and more suspicious
finding.

## Not a regression in any gate

434s and 586s are both well under the old 900s cap, and the tier is green
throughout. Nothing is broken. This is a signal that a balance change had a
measurable size, filed so the size is on the record rather than inferred later
from a slow test run.

## Also noticed, separate and smaller

`godot/scripts/game_manager.gd:130` calls `VerificationTracker.enable_debug()`
unconditionally on every game start -- not gated on a debug build, a test
harness, or a config flag. That is where the sim tier's ~4-5M `print()` lines
per run come from, and it means shipped player builds are doing the same
per-RNG-call string formatting and stdout write. Worth its own look; it is not
the cause of anything in #1181, just adjacent.

## Provenance

Measured 2026-08-09 while fixing #1181. Method and the full old-vs-new
comparison are in PR #1192.

issues.title: fix(leaderboard): the Operator name was collected and never carried anywhere -- two identity fields, and a truncation that stops amputating
issues.body:
Branched from `fix/leaderboard-visibility-set` (PR #1173, still open at time of writing), not from `main`.

## What the board displays today vs what is collected

Measured against the live `(weekly-2026-w32, L4)` board on 2026-08-08, not assumed:

| | Collected by the game | Reaches the board |
|---|---|---|
| Operator name (`GameConfig.player_name`, default `"Researcher"`) | Yes -- persisted, loaded, settable, and asked for by the #1133 prompt under the label `Operator:` | **No. Nowhere. No code path ever moved it.** |
| Lab name (`GameConfig.lab_name`) | Yes, with a generator and a Reroll button | Yes -- in a field named `player_name` |

The receiving field declared itself:

```gdscript
var player_name: String  # Lab name
```

A field whose own comment admitted it was misnamed, feeding a public column of the same wrong name. That is the silent-wrongness pattern in a schema, and the website renders that column.

`docs/LEADERBOARD_WEBSITE_INTEGRATION.md:148` documented the same thing as if it were fine: `` `player_name` | string | Lab name displayed on leaderboard ``.

## The truncation limit: 40 bytes, measured

I did not trust the figure of 40. I fetched the live board and measured it:

```
GET https://api.pdoom1.com/score_api.php?seed=weekly-2026-w32&version=L4&limit=50

'GRIM (Global Risk Intervention Mechanism'  len=40   <- Pip, amputated
'GRIM'                                      len=4
'GRIM'                                      len=4
''                                          len=0
''                                          len=0
```

Submitted `"GRIM (Global Risk Intervention Mechanism)"` = 41 bytes. Stored = 40. **The server ate exactly one byte, silently.** The limit is 40, confirmed by the boundary rather than by the doc.

Two things that measurement adds beyond the number:

- The cut is **byte-wise**. A non-ASCII name (a player typing an accented name) can be split mid-codepoint and stored as invalid UTF-8. Fitting client-side prevents that too.
- **Two of the five live rows have an EMPTY name.** `_has_submittable_identity()` requires both fields non-empty, so those rows did not come through the current consent path. I have not chased this; flagging it as unexplained, not fixed.

`score_api.php` is deployed server-side and is **not in `pdoom1-website` or any repo on this machine** (I checked). The only truncation code in that repo is `bug-submit.php`, unrelated. So the limit cannot be raised from here.

## The decision, and what I did with it

Pip ruled mid-task, so this PR builds the answer rather than a card:

> "can we submit both? players will collide on lab names and player names are also cool because then a player can have different labs?"

**BOTH, as separate values.** Lab names collide -- that is *why* the #1133 generator exists -- so a lab alone cannot identify a person; and one Operator running several labs over several months is a feature that a single conflated field would destroy permanently.

He also said *"I'm not asking for it now it just feels silly"* -- naming the absurdity, not setting a deadline. So this PR stops short of anything that migrates live data or needs a server change.

## What is implemented

1. **The field name and its contents now agree.** `ScoreEntry.player_name` -> `ScoreEntry.lab_name`, plus a new `ScoreEntry.operator_name`. The old name is **gone, not repurposed** -- a stale reader errors loudly instead of silently returning the wrong name. Two pre-existing tests broke on exactly that, which is the property working rather than a regression.

   The JSON **key** stays `player_name`, because every local board file on disk and every row on the live board uses it. The GDScript field is honest; the wire key is the frozen contract, now documented as misnamed.

2. **Truncation is legible and client-side.** `Leaderboard.fit_board_name()` -- pure, static, unit-tested -- fits to the measured 40-byte budget, cutting on a word boundary and marking the cut with ASCII `...`. Applied in `to_wire_dict()`, so the server's `substr` never fires.

   Pip's lab now goes up as `GRIM (Global Risk Intervention...` instead of `GRIM (Global Risk Intervention Mechanism`.

   A name that fits passes through untouched -- a cut mark on an uncut name is its own small lie.

3. **The prompt no longer overpromises.** `IDENTITY_PROMPT_BOARD_NOTE` states that the global board shows the Lab name and the Operator name is saved with the run locally. The prompt was collecting two values while one of them went nowhere.

4. **Local/remote split made explicit.** `to_dict()` = the full local record (both names). `to_wire_dict()` = exactly the frozen server contract, name pre-fitted, `operator_name` **deliberately omitted**.

## What I deliberately did NOT do

- **Did not send `operator_name` on the wire.** The server's tolerance for unknown keys is unmeasured and a rejected POST loses a score. Sending it blind at 01:00 against a live public board is the wrong trade.
- **Did not touch a single row on the live board.**
- **Did not render both names on the leaderboard screen.** Remote rows will never carry an operator until the server does, so the screen would render a ragged mix.
- No `version.txt` / `ladder_version.txt` / tag change. Ladder stays L4; the board key does not move. Nothing here touches RNG, economy or replay determinism.

## What happens to the rows already on the live board

`from_dict` defaults `operator_name` to `""` for any row lacking it -- which is every row that exists today, local and remote.

- Existing rows present as **lab-only, rendered honestly**. No backfill.
- Backfilling the lab into the operator field would **fabricate an identity** -- asserting that a human is named "GRIM". There is a test asserting it does not happen.
- Pip's amputated row stays amputated. Fixing it is a server-side edit; only future submissions are fitted.

## Open, for coordination (pdoom1-website / API territory)

1. **Add a second identity field to the score API** (schema + endpoint + public rendering) so the Operator name can be carried. This PR has the client value sitting ready.
2. **Either raise the 40-byte limit or make the server's cut legible**, and return the stored value so the client can tell the player what actually landed. The client now fits to 40 regardless.
3. **Why do two live rows have empty names?** Unexplained.

Written up in `docs/LEADERBOARD_WEBSITE_INTEGRATION.md` so it survives this PR.

## Red/green proof

Every guard proven to fail first, against the real defect behaviour -- not merely against a missing symbol.

The compile-level red (API absent) was real but weak, so I staged the seam with `fit_board_name` **deliberately reproducing the server's own `substr`**, making the guards fail behaviourally with counts:

| | Tests | Failures |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline, before any change | 1233 | 0 |
| **RED** -- guards vs. defect behaviour | 1252 | **9** |
| **GREEN** -- after the fix | 1252 | **0** |

The 9 red, named:

- `test_the_live_amputation_is_never_reproduced` -- reproduced the exact live public string
- `test_cut_names_break_on_a_word_boundary_when_one_is_available`
- `test_a_single_unbroken_word_still_gets_cut_rather_than_dropped`
- `test_wire_dict_fits_the_board_limit_so_the_server_never_cuts`
- `test_game_over_screen_submits_the_operator_name_too` -- names the defect site, `game_over_screen.gd`
- `test_identity_prompt_is_honest_about_what_reaches_the_board`
- `test_prompt_retrofit_applies_both_names_to_the_pending_entry`
- `test_rename_entry_renames_in_place_name_only` (pre-existing, red on the rename)
- `test_parse_board_entries_ok` (pre-existing, red on the rename)

The last two are the rename proving itself total.

Fast gate: `python scripts/run_godot_tests.py --quick --ci-mode --min-tests 300` -> 1252 tests, 0 fail, 125/125 files collected. Simulation tier not run: nothing here touches simulation, economy or replay.

## Containment

Every Godot invocation ran under `APPDATA=C:/Users/Pip/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/godot-iso-identity`, proven before any test run:

```
USER_DATA_DIR=C:/Users/Pip/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/godot-iso-identity/Godot/app_userdata/P(Doom)
```

Nothing under Pip's Roaming profile was read or written.

issues.title: Ladder eligibility must be visible BEFORE the run starts, not delivered at death (ruled by Pip 2026-08-07)
issues.body:
**Ruling by Pip, 2026-08-07 ~23:30, during the v0.14.0 playtest:**

> "If we're setting up a game that isn't eligible for a ladder submission, we should know before we start the game"

## The rule

**Ladder eligibility is a property the player can see BEFORE committing to a run, not a verdict delivered at death.**

Today a run's eligibility is only surfaced at game over (`game_over_screen.gd:266`), and mid-run at first Alpha Tools use. Both are after the player has invested. Pip invested **147 turns** tonight before discovering a run produced nothing -- and the current design gives a player no way to know in advance.

## Why this is not just a nicety

Eligibility is already determined by state that exists **before turn 1**:

- `GameConfig.scenario_id` -- chosen pre-game
- difficulty (locked to Standard for league runs, #1058)
- the board key `(seed, ladder_epoch)` -- both known at setup
- Alpha Tools is the only input that arrives mid-run, and it is one-way, so "eligible so far" is honest and never becomes eligible again

So the information exists at setup. Nothing is being computed early; it is simply not being shown.

**And it would have made tonight's blocker visible in seconds instead of hours.** A pre-game readout would have told Pip immediately which of his three runs the game believed were rankable, splitting "the run was unranked" from "the submit path is broken" without any code reading at all. An eligibility indicator is a diagnostic instrument as much as a UI feature.

## What this asks for

1. **A clear, non-decorative eligibility statement on the pre-game / setup screen**, before the player commits. Something a person reads without hunting: whether this run will count, and if not, why not, in one line.
2. **Consistency with the existing tellings.** Alpha Tools already warns at the toggle, at first use, and at game over (decision card 2026-08-01). This adds a fourth position -- BEFORE -- and it should use the same vocabulary so a player reads one concept, not four.
3. **The honest wording problem worth designing around:** at setup the truthful statement is conditional -- "this run is eligible, and will stop being eligible if you use dev tools". Avoid promising a submission that a later action revokes. Pip's own standing preference is that the player should be told what is prevented and why, in plain words.

## Scope note

This is a DESIGN issue, filed separately from the live blocker (a clean 147-turn run submitting nothing, under diagnosis). **Do not let this absorb that.** If the diagnosis finds the submit path is broken, fixing it does not discharge this issue, and vice versa -- one is a defect, this is a missing affordance, and either could exist without the other.

## Related

- `game_over_screen.gd:266` -- current, and only, player-facing eligibility gate
- `GameConfig.is_ranked_run()` / `effective_difficulty()` -- the named accessors this would read
- `#1058` -- difficulty locked to Standard for comparable league runs
- `#1060` -- scenarios lock you out of the board, with an explicit pre-pick warning. **That warning is the precedent this generalises**: scenarios already tell the player before they commit. Alpha Tools and everything else do not.

issues.title: Simulation tier cannot be run locally on Windows -- 15-min hardcoded timeout, and a timeout reports as '0 tests, 0 fail'
issues.body:
Found while cutting v0.14.0 / L4, on the one release where the simulation tier is
the tier that matters (the cut forks the ladder because #1137 retimed the event
deck, and replay/determinism is exactly what this tier guards).

## The measurement

`python scripts/run_godot_tests.py --simulation --ci-mode --min-tests 80` on the
Windows dev machine, in a clean worktree at `origin/main` (`1795cd12`):

```
[TEST] Running 'simulation' tests in res://tests/unit/simulation (8 files on disk)
[FAIL] Tests timed out after 15 minutes!
[TOTALS] simulation: 0 tests, 0 fail (FAIL)
```

Run three times, ~15 min each:

| tree | stdout | result |
|---|---|---|
| v0.14.0 release branch | pipe | timeout, 0 tests |
| v0.14.0 release branch | redirected to a file | timeout, 0 tests |
| **unmodified `origin/main`** | redirected to a file | **timeout, 0 tests** |

The third row is the point: **main alone reproduces it.** The epoch cut is
exonerated by that A/B. This is pre-existing.

Meanwhile the same tier is **green in GitHub Actions on Ubuntu**, including on
the #1137 commit itself (run `31091011227`, job "Simulation Tests") and on the
latest main run (`31130859770`). The workflow passes `--min-tests 80`, so a
zero-test run would have failed the job; it did not.

## Two separate defects

**1. The tier cannot be run locally on Windows at all.**
15 minutes is hardcoded -- `scripts/run_godot_tests.py:329`,
`subprocess.run(..., timeout=900)` -- with no CLI flag to raise it. So a
developer on this machine has no way to get a result, only a timeout. Every
local run of this tier is a guaranteed 15-minute wait for nothing.

**2. A timeout reports as `0 tests` rather than as "unknown".**
`[TOTALS] simulation: 0 tests, 0 fail (FAIL)` reads like a measurement. It is
not one -- no test was observed to pass or fail. This is the repo's house
failure mode (silent wrongness) wearing a green-adjacent number: "0 fail" is
literally true and completely misleading.

## Probable cause of the slowness (partially diagnosed, not proven)

Running GUT directly against `res://tests/unit/simulation` floods stdout with one
line per RNG draw:

```
[VerificationTracker] RNG: event_hist_arxiv_218ce086ce67d573=0.948207 -> 69befb4da53334e3...
```

Sampled mid-run, the Godot process had **16.2 minutes wall clock against 7.9
seconds of user CPU** -- it is blocked on I/O, not computing. The print is
`debug_mode`-gated (`godot/autoload/verification_tracker.gd:225-226`), so it is
test-only and does **not** ship to players; a sim test turns it on deliberately.

Caveat, stated because it undercuts the theory: redirecting stdout to a file
instead of a pipe did **not** fix it. So console/pipe I/O is at most part of the
story and something else is also slow or stuck. Not chased further -- a release
was in flight.

## Asks

1. Add a `--timeout` flag to `run_godot_tests.py` so the tier can at least be
   run to completion locally.
2. Make a timeout report as **UNKNOWN / DID NOT RUN**, never as `0 tests, 0 fail`.
   A gate that cannot distinguish "nothing failed" from "nothing ran" is the
   exact defect #640 fixed for the fast gate; the slow tier still has it.
3. Find the real Windows slowness. Start by checking whether the per-RNG-draw
   debug print can be buffered or suppressed under GUT, then bisect the 8 files
   in `godot/tests/unit/simulation/` for the one that dominates.

## Consequence accepted for v0.14.0

v0.14.0 shipped with the simulation tier verified **only in CI**, not locally,
with that stated plainly in the handover rather than smoothed over. The fast gate
was green locally both before and after the change (1212 tests, 0 failures,
119/119 files -- identical counts).

issues.title: godot/data/historical_events.json carries two mojibake titles; the upstream repair cannot reach a hand-carried copy
issues.body:
**The shipped event snapshot carries two mojibake titles.**

Filed by the `pdoom-data` seat. Measured on `Bort` at 2026-08-07 17:0x AEST, twice: once by an independent scan, then again by hand before filing.

*(Rewritten 17:2x -- the first version of this body was mechanically derived from the sibling report filed as `pdoom1-website#282` and carried phrasing that belonged to that repo. This is the pdoom1-specific version.)*

## The finding

`godot/data/historical_events.json`, the 1,194-record snapshot taken from `pdoom-data`:

    uk_ai_safety_to_security_2025
      is        : 'UK AI Safety Institute \xe2†’ AI Security Institute'
      should be : 'UK AI Safety Institute -> AI Security Institute'

    us_aisi_to_caisi_2025
      is        : 'US AISI \xe2†’ Center for AI Standards and Innovation'
      should be : 'US AISI -> Center for AI Standards and Innovation'

`\xe2†’` is the bytes `E2 86 92` -- `U+2192` RIGHTWARDS ARROW in UTF-8 -- read as CP1252. Single-level mangling; the recovered strings contain nothing further suspicious.

Whether a player sees these depends on whether either event surfaces in play, which is a pdoom1 question rather than a pdoom-data one.

## Use `->`, not the recovered arrow

Upstream `pdoom-data` repaired these on 2026-08-06 to the ASCII `->`, because that repo is ASCII-only and its repair rule is an explicit substitution map that errors on unmapped characters rather than guessing. Writing back the reconstructed `U+2192` would leave the copies disagreeing in a **new** way rather than the old one. Verified upstream on `main`:

    'UK AI Safety Institute -> AI Security Institute'

## Why the upstream fix did not reach you

`pdoom-data` shipped a transcoding gate today (`pdoom-data#69`). It scans every JSON and JSONL under its own `data/` tree, and **it cannot see this file by construction** -- `godot/data/historical_events.json` is a frozen hand-carried copy that does not regenerate, which is exactly why the 08-06 repair did not propagate.

So the gate protects the source and not the consumer. This seat has no standing to choose pdoom1's answer, but the two available shapes are: the snapshot becomes a **refreshed artifact** with a recorded provenance and a re-sync step, or pdoom1 runs its **own** transcoding check over `godot/data/` in CI. They are not exclusive, and only the first stops it recurring.

Detection rule if you want it standalone -- and deliberately reimplement rather than import, so that a defect in one implementation is not invisible to both:

> a string is corrupt if it contains `U+00C2`, `U+00C3` or `U+00E2` **and** `s.encode('cp1252').decode('utf-8')` succeeds and differs. The result is what it should have been.

Two traps, both of which cost this seat time today: split JSONL on `\n` only, because `str.splitlines()` also breaks on `U+2028` and `U+0085`, which occur inside string values in these corpora and will fragment records into false findings; and print findings `ascii()`-escaped, because a Windows console re-mangles mojibake on output and a genuinely corrupt string can print back looking correct.

## Scope, measured rather than assumed

A cross-repo sweep today scanned 536 files in `pdoom1` (`godot/data/` and `docs/`), 347 in `pdoom1-website`, and 68 markdown files in `coordination`. **Every file on disk decoded cleanly as UTF-8**; the corruption is inside string values, not in file encoding. Findings were exactly these two records, in this file and in `pdoom1-website/public/data/events.json` (filed as `pdoom1-website#282`). `pdoom1/docs/` is clean. `coordination` is clean.

## Related

`pdoom-data#68` (the finding), `pdoom-data#69` (the gate), `pdoom-data#52` (the missing producer that surfaced it), `pdoom1-website#282` (the same two records in the site's served copy), `coordination#10` (the transcoding species).

issues.title: Review: what does pdoom1 actually want from pdoom-data? (measured inventory, no proposal)
issues.body:
**Raised at Pip's direction** (`pdoom-data#55`): pdoom1 decides what it wants from pdoom-data, and pdoom-data then supplies that. Direction of authority is pdoom1 -> pdoom-data. So this issue carries measurements and questions, and deliberately **no proposal**.

Findings come from a read-only static audit of this repo plus JSON measurement of the corpus. The game was not run; anything runtime-dependent is flagged.

---

## The question

**What do you actually want a pdoom-data event to carry?**

Everything below exists so that can be answered against facts rather than against either side's guesses. If the answer is "much less than we currently send", that is a good outcome and cheap to deliver.

---

## What pdoom1 reads today

`godot/data/historical_events.json`, 1,194 records. Every raw-record access in the tree is in one file, `godot/autoload/event_service.gd`.

**Nine of thirteen fields are read.** Never accessed anywhere: `sources` (1,194 records, none empty), `tags`, `impacts[].condition` (3,636 entries, all null), `source_id`. `pdoom_impact` is copied onto the transformed event and then read by nothing; 1,187 of its 1,194 values are null.

Derived keys written onto the game event that nothing downstream reads: `eligibility_start`, `eligibility_end`, `trigger_mode`, `historical`, `significance`, `source_data` (which carries a full copy of the raw record).

## The number that should shape the answer

**98.3% of the corpus never reaches a decision window.** `_is_flavour_event` (`event_service.gd:491-497`) demotes every `technical_research_breakthrough` and every `arxiv*` id to `delivery_tier: "feed"`. Feed items render as one grey line and **their options are never presented and their effects never applied**.

1,174 of 1,194 records are inert beyond `id`, `title`, `category`, `year`. Twenty can open a window; one is then dropped by the start-year filter.

**So the decision surface pdoom1 gets from 1,194 curated events is nineteen records.**

That is the single most decision-relevant fact in this audit. If pdoom-data is supplying 1,194 records to fill nineteen slots, the contract question is not "which fields" but "which records, and chosen how".

## Rarity is not carrying the meaning your curve file assumes

Corpus: rare 1,076, common 77, legendary 41.

**All 41 `legendary` records are in the arxiv/flavour stream** — so the tier meaning "always fires at its historical date, key story beat" is applied exclusively to records that are then demoted to a grey line. The nineteen records that can open a window are seventeen `common` and three `rare`. **Zero legendary.**

Cause, measured in pdoom-data: `rarity` is an exact `text_length > 20000` threshold on a field that is not carried into the output (`pdoom-data#51`). Zero violations in 1,129 records. Correlation with the visible description length is r = -0.0065.

Boundary case nobody validates: `_get_rarity_settings` tests `_rarity_curves.has(rarity)`, and `rarity_curves.json` has top-level keys `default_rarity`, `year_trigger`, `_description`, `_note`. A record with `rarity: "year_trigger"` would pass that test and return the wrong dict. No such record exists today.

## Significance discriminates almost nothing

`significance` is summed from `abs(change)` across `impacts` and scales every generated option's effects (`event_service.gd:500-528`, `:587-590`).

**1,166 of 1,194 records score exactly 6.** Whole-corpus distribution `{6: 1166, 8: 4, 9: 6, 10: 18}`.

## `impacts` are not inert, and three of your docs say they are

`events.gd:290-310` intercepts a literal `doom` key and reroutes it into `doom_system.add_stream_input("panic", ...)`. Its own comment names **pdoom-data-derived events as the sole remaining producer of literal doom effects**.

`WS3_FINISH_OR_DROP.md:280-282`, `TECH_DEBT_BURNDOWN.md:78-79` and `resource_accessor.gd:73-76` all still describe that path as an inert sink. Flagging as a doc/code disagreement rather than asserting which is intended.

Meanwhile pdoom-data's supplied vocabulary — `vibey_doom`, `stress`, `burnout_risk` — maps onto `doom` via `variable_mapping.json`, which is precisely what ADR-0015 outlaws. It survives only because of that reroute. Three variables are silently dropped as unmapped: `ethics_risk` (16), `technical_debt` (12), `media_reputation` (4). They still count toward significance.

Path B (literal effects) reaches gameplay for **seven records only** — the `funding_catastrophe` branch. The other twelve window-tier records build effects from `significance` alone.

## Three asks already on your record that pdoom-data does not answer

Not new requests from us. These are pdoom1's own documents.

**ADR-0012** (accepted 2026-07-12) names four event-content fields: *class, expiry N, response-expected flag, carrying-cost hook*. pdoom-data supplies none; everything defaults to `deferrable`.

**pdoom1#630 / `UI_FEATURES_STACK.md:39-44`** — the feed drowning in `hist_arxiv`, "the ENTIRE hist_arxiv deck fires, 200+ entries in event_cooldowns". `SESSION_STATUS_2026-07-17.md:36-37` names pdoom-data's salience tiers as the principled fix. pdoom-data has that field on its candidate feed (`salience_tier_by_profile`, A 172 / B 687 / C 1717 / D 858) but **not on `all_events.json`**, which is the collection you read.

**`TRIUMVIRATE_METABOLIC_CYCLE.md:90-116`** (proposed, not ratified) asks for monthly facts-only packs and states the split: *pdoom-data owns the fact schema, pdoom1 owns the shaping schema*. pdoom-data has since ratified its side of that as ADR-007 and ADR-008.

## One thing pdoom-data will not do, and why it is in your interest

DQ-21 is resolved and its vocabulary is live — `general_capability`, `frontier_capability`, `global_compute`, `dedicated_ai_compute`, `political_pressure`, `ambient_risk`, `global_alarm`, `global_panic`, accepted at `events.gd:315-337`. pdoom-data could encode those names directly.

**ADR-007 in pdoom-data says it should not**, and the reason favours you: if we encode `frontier_capability` and you later rename or split it, every exported pack already in the wild silently means the wrong thing — no error, no failed parse, just numbers attached to a concept that no longer exists. An external taxonomy plus a mapping table on your side keeps your vocabulary yours to revise as often as the design needs.

If you would rather have your names directly, say so and we will do it — but that is the trade being made.

## Also outstanding, unrelated to schema

`pdoom1#1098` — 42 records in the bundled copy still carry un-redacted email addresses. `scripts/sync_from_pdoom_data.sh` reads directories that no longer exist in pdoom-data and has never successfully run, so there is no path for upstream corrections to arrive.

## Could not determine

Whether any of this holds at runtime; everything is static tracing plus JSON measurement. Why `historical_events.json` is a hand-commit rather than a sync output. Whether the "inert sink" docs are simply stale post-#985 or describe a path not traced.

Refs `pdoom-data#43`, `pdoom-data#51`, `pdoom-data#52`, `pdoom-data#55`, `pdoom1#630`, `pdoom1#1052`, `pdoom1#1098`, `pdoom1-website#240`.

issues.title: docs: ladder epoch columns are off by one from v0.14 down in ROADMAP.md and RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md
issues.body:
Extracted from #1018 before it closes, per `docs/ISSUE_MINING_2026-08-06.md`. Verified live on `main` at 2026-08-06.

## The defect

Two published documents map version to ladder epoch, and both are off by one from v0.14 down:

- `docs/ROADMAP.md:47` -- `| v0.14 | Aug 7 | L3 | Per-tick & People (prov.) | ... |`
- `docs/RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md:89` -- `| **Aug 7** | **Fri** | **Theme v0.14 ...** | Epoch+Seed | 0.14 / **L3** | **Yes** |`

L3 was spent mid-month by #982 and the shipped build is already `0.13.2 / L3`. So `v0.14 -> L3` claims the next epoch will NOT fork the ladder, when by both documents' own rules it must. Every row below inherits the shift (`v0.15 -> L4` should be L5, and so on).

## Why it is worth fixing rather than tolerating

The ladder epoch is the board key. `tools/sync_version.py --check` gates pre-commit and CI precisely because a silent version drift forks the leaderboard -- CLAUDE.md calls that fatal. These two tables are the human-readable half of the same contract, and they currently disagree with the shipped constant. Anyone planning the Aug 7 cut from either table plans the wrong board.

Cheap: two table columns, plus a scan for other places the mapping is restated.

## Provenance

Found by the #1018 ADR-supersession scan on 2026-07-29 and recorded there as one of six collisions. #1018 is being closed and folded into #1049; #1049 is a broader ADR-honesty issue raised from the website side and does **not** carry the collision matrix. This one is live, so it is filed separately rather than left in a folded issue.

One of the six has since self-resolved: the stale `game_config.gd:159-160` runtime comment ("Epoch L1 == the current ruleset", above a const reading `"3"`) is gone from `main`.

## Adjacent, from the same scan, if someone is in these files anyway

`L<n>` is overloaded: ladder epochs L1/L2/L3 versus the distribution update ladder L0-L3. Same notation, unrelated meanings, both spoken in league week. #1018 asked for that namespace to be ruled. Worth one sentence in `RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md` disambiguating them.

Source: #1018 (closing). Related: #1049 (the broader ADR pass), #982, `docs/GLOSSARY.md`.

issues.title: events: four measured defects in the pdoom-data ingest path (rarity boundary case, dropped-but-counted variables, inert-sink doc disagreement, constant significance)
issues.body:
Extracted from #1102 before it closes, per `docs/ISSUE_MINING_2026-08-06.md`.

#1102 is a measured, read-only audit of what pdoom1 gets from pdoom-data, and its headline question was answered by the memo at `docs/memos/MEMO_2026-08-04_1106-and-1102.html`. But #1102 is memo-shaped, and four **code-level defects in THIS repo** are buried inside it. The memo carries the headline numbers (1,194 records / nineteen decision records / rarity / significance) and does not carry these. They are measurements, so re-deriving them means redoing the audit.

None of these were run against a live game -- #1102 states everything is static tracing plus JSON measurement. Treat each as "verify, then fix", not "fix".

## 1. `_get_rarity_settings` has a boundary case that returns the wrong dict

`_get_rarity_settings` tests `_rarity_curves.has(rarity)`. `rarity_curves.json` has top-level keys `default_rarity`, `year_trigger`, `_description`, `_note`. **A record with `rarity: "year_trigger"` would pass that test and be handed a configuration dict that is not a rarity curve.** No such record exists in the corpus today, so this is latent, not live -- but the corpus is externally supplied and the check is a `has()` against a dict that mixes data with metadata.

Fix shape: validate against an explicit allowlist of rarity names, not against key presence in a file that also holds `_description`.

## 2. Three supplied variables are silently dropped but still inflate `significance`

`ethics_risk` (16 records), `technical_debt` (12), `media_reputation` (4) arrive in `impacts` and are dropped as unmapped -- **and still count toward the `significance` sum**, which scales every generated option's effect magnitude (`event_service.gd:500-528`, `:587-590`).

So an event whose only impacts are unmapped variables produces a larger effect than an event with no impacts, for no reason a designer could see. Silent, and it moves numbers.

Fix shape: decide whether unmapped variables should map, be rejected loudly at load, or be excluded from the significance sum. Any of the three beats the current behaviour.

## 3. Three documents describe an active code path as an inert sink

`events.gd:290-310` intercepts a literal `doom` key in `impacts` and reroutes it into `doom_system.add_stream_input("panic", ...)`. Its own comment names pdoom-data-derived events as the sole remaining producer of literal doom effects.

These three all still say that path is dead:
- `WS3_FINISH_OR_DROP.md:280-282`
- `TECH_DEBT_BURNDOWN.md:78-79`
- `resource_accessor.gd:73-76`

#1102 flagged this as a doc/code disagreement without asserting which is intended. Someone has to rule. Note the ADR-0015 angle: pdoom-data's `vibey_doom` / `stress` / `burnout_risk` map onto `doom` via `variable_mapping.json`, which is precisely what ADR-0015 outlaws, and the mapping survives ONLY because of that reroute. So "which document is right" is really "is ADR-0015 being honoured here".

## 4. `significance` discriminates almost nothing

**1,166 of 1,194 records score exactly 6.** Whole-corpus distribution `{6: 1166, 8: 4, 9: 6, 10: 18}`. It is used as a scaling multiplier on option effects, so in practice it is a constant with 28 exceptions. Either it should carry meaning or it should stop being a multiplier -- but it should not silently be a constant wearing the costume of a signal.

Related: the same section of #1102 measures that **all 41 `legendary` records are in the demoted arxiv/flavour stream**, so the tier meaning "always fires at its historical date, key story beat" is applied exclusively to records rendered as one grey line. The nineteen records that can open a decision window are seventeen `common` and three `rare`. **Zero legendary.** That is a content-authoring fact worth knowing before anyone tunes rarity.

## Also worth carrying forward

pdoom-data has `salience_tier_by_profile` on its candidate feed (A 172 / B 687 / C 1717 / D 858) but **not on `all_events.json`**, which is the collection pdoom1 reads. `SESSION_STATUS_2026-07-17.md:36-37` names salience tiers as the principled fix for the feed drowning in `hist_arxiv` (#630). The field exists upstream and is not on the surface we consume.

Source: #1102 (closing; headline answered by the 08-04 memo). Refs `pdoom-data#43`, `#51`, `#52`, `#55`, `pdoom1#630`, `#1052`, `#1098`.

issues.title: content: promote the real-people/real-venue content guardrail from a closing issue comment to a tracked doc
issues.body:
Extracted from #803 before it closes, per `docs/ISSUE_MINING_2026-08-06.md`. #803 (revisit ADR-0014 conferences) is being retired because its days-granularity premise was overtaken by the turn=ONE MONTH ruling (#1125). But its comment thread carries a content-safety ruling that has nothing to do with conference granularity, is not recorded in any document, and applies to a large and growing amount of generated content.

`grep -rln "real named|wrongdoing|fictional venue" docs/` returns nothing on `main` at 2026-08-06. This ruling exists in exactly one place: a GitHub comment on an issue about to be closed.

## The ruling (Pip, 2026-07-22, verbatim)

> **Governing principle:** NEVER imply wrongdoing by a single real human, or realistic institutional negligence by a real named entity, in any period between sim-start and modern day. Historical contributions to AI capabilities are NOT morally judged -- only PLAYER and RIVAL actions carry moral weight.

> **The differential (solved by simple writing):** a mishap is fine when it is distinctively WEIRD / fantastical (clearly not a realistic real-world failing); NOT fine when it reads as plausible real-world negligence or wrongdoing attributable to the real named venue/person.

> - OK: ninjas rappel through the ceiling and steal a briefcase.
> - OK: the return flight is delayed by a doomstorm.
> - NOT OK: a conference volunteer pickpockets an attendee in line (implies the real event had thieving staff).
> - NOT OK: the venue roof leaks from poor maintenance (implies real venue negligence).

> **Easter eggs:** fictional-researcher vignettes are the sweet spot -- e.g. a low-impulse-control researcher returns 2 days late "worse for wear and glazed", minus their Settlers of Catan, plus a USB of bitcoin they cannot remember.

And the accepted pushback recorded in the same comment, applying Pip's own rule back to a suggestion of his:

> keep such pegs FICTIONAL. Naming a real recent person (e.g. a real convicted financier) reintroduces exactly the real-human-wrongdoing risk the rule forbids -- even as a joke, even about someone with real convictions. Keep the vignette; drop the real name. The fictional researcher is funnier AND zero-risk.

## Why this needs a home

The game ships 1,194 historical records naming real people and real organisations, wants conference data populated from real events, and has a stated intent to generate flavour, antagonists, scandals and travel mishaps on top of that. The rule is the thing standing between "juicy flavour" and a defamation-shaped problem, and right now the only way to learn it is to have been in the thread.

It also generalises past conferences: it is really a rule about the boundary between the historical corpus (neutral, unjudged) and the fictional layer (where moral weight lives).

## Ask

Promote it to a tracked doc -- `docs/game-design/CONTENT_SAFETY_RULES.md` or a section in `DESIGN_PHILOSOPHY.md`, whichever Pip prefers -- keeping the four worked examples, because the examples are what make the differential usable by someone writing copy at speed. Cross-reference it from wherever event/flavour content gets authored, and from the pdoom-data contract if real-entity records flow in from there.

Source: #803 (closing as overtaken). Related: ADR-0014, #1102 (the pdoom-data corpus), DQ-16.

issues.title: ui(input): sweep the '_input shortcut + focused Control' double-fire shape across godot/scripts/ui
issues.body:
Extracted from #1032 before it closes, per `docs/ISSUE_MINING_2026-08-06.md`. PR #1144 fixed `config_confirmation.gd`. #1032 explicitly declined to scope the sweep, and said why:

> Wider point worth a moment's thought rather than a rule: this file is one of several that hand-roll `_input` keyboard shortcuts alongside a focused control. The same "shortcut handler plus focused button" shape exists elsewhere in `godot/scripts/ui/` and each instance needs the same discipline. Not proposing a sweep in this issue; noting that **the shape is the bug, not the file.**

## The mechanism, restated

A script handles a key in `_input()` and does not call `get_viewport().set_input_as_handled()`. A Godot `Button` that holds focus activates on the `ui_accept` action, which ENTER is bound to by default. The same keypress therefore reaches BOTH paths and the handler runs twice.

In `config_confirmation.gd` the observable damage was `GameConfig.increment_games_played()` running twice per keyboard launch -- so the statistic was inflated ~2x for keyboard players and 1x for mouse players, incoherent across the population rather than merely wrong by a constant. That is the interesting part: the consequence was not the double navigation (absorbed by `SceneTransition`'s guard) but a quietly corrupted counter that nothing would ever flag.

## Ask

1. Enumerate every `_input` / `_gui_input` handler under `godot/scripts/ui/` that responds to ENTER, SPACE, or ESC while a Control in the same scene can hold focus.
2. For each: decide whether the double-fire is harmless (no competing handler wired) or damaging (a side effect that is not idempotent), and mark the event handled either way.
3. Look specifically for non-idempotent side effects -- counters, appends, submissions, persisted config writes -- because those are the ones that fail silently.

Not urgent. Worth doing as one pass rather than one bug at a time, because the second instance will present as a different symptom entirely.

Source: #1032 (closing, first instance fixed in PR #1144). Related: #1027 (silent wrongness), #1120 (keyboard/navigation surface -- coordinate before touching input handling).

issues.title: core: pending_events is an unguarded public queue -- give it one validated entry point (class fix behind #1134)
issues.body:
Extracted from #1134 before it closes, per `docs/ISSUE_MINING_2026-08-06.md`. PR #1144 fixed the instance -- F3 event injection now refuses outside `ACTION_SELECTION`, with a legible refusal and an exhaustive phase test. This is the class fix that #1134 flagged and deliberately left out of scope.

## #1134's own words

> The deeper version, worth considering separately: `pending_events` is a queue any caller can push to with no validation. This is the first caller found doing it wrongly; it is unlikely to be the last. A single guarded entry point would make the class impossible rather than this instance.

## The shape of the problem

`gm.state.pending_events.append(event)` is a raw array append on a public field. The invariant that matters -- an event may only be enqueued in a phase that will drain it -- currently lives in ONE caller (`debug_overlay.gd`, after #1144). Any other caller, present or future, gets no help. The failure mode when it goes wrong is not an error: it is a run that cannot advance, which is the worst-behaved outcome in this codebase's taxonomy (see #1027).

## Ask

Route all enqueues through a single named method on GameState or GameManager that:

1. checks the current phase can drain the queue, and refuses otherwise;
2. returns a result the caller can act on rather than failing silently;
3. names explicitly any phases that may legitimately accept an event for LATER draining, if such phases exist.

Then make `pending_events` unreachable for direct append from outside (or, if GDScript makes that awkward, add a test that greps for `pending_events.append` outside the guarded module -- the repo already uses that pattern for scene navigation via `tools/check_scene_nav.py`).

## Scope note

Worth checking at the same time whether other queue-shaped fields on GameState have the same exposure. The generator here is "a public array that a state machine drains", not "events specifically".

Source: #1134 (closing, instance fixed in PR #1144). Related: #1027, #1112 (dev-tool versus alpha-tool boundary).

issues.title: release: add a BEHAVIOURAL build-identity check to the release checklist (a feature the old build cannot have)
issues.body:
Extracted from #1067 before it closes, per `docs/ISSUE_MINING_2026-08-06.md`. #1067's headline defect (CI shipped a stale `build_stamp.txt`) IS fixed -- CI exports route through `tools/build_release.py` now. This is the "bonus" half of that issue, which was never actioned and is not recorded anywhere else.

## The observation, verbatim from #1067

> Build identity was confirmed in about fifteen seconds behaviourally -- open the scenario dropdown, see the amber `[!] NOT RANKED` warning that only exists in code merged at 16:15 that day. **A feature that cannot exist in the previous version is a stronger identity check than any string the build prints about itself.** Worth writing into the release checklist regardless of whether the stamp gets fixed.

## Why it is worth a ticket

The stamp is a string the artifact prints ABOUT itself. It cannot fail loudly -- when wrong it reports a plausible commit on a plausible date, which is exactly how it sent someone three weeks in the wrong direction on 2026-07-31. Every fix to the stamp is a fix to a self-report. A behavioural check is orthogonal evidence: it cannot be faked by a stale file, a stale cache, or a wrong upload, because the feature either exists in the running binary or it does not.

## Verified absent

`grep -niE "NOT RANKED|behaviour|behavior|feature that cannot exist|identity" .github/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` returns nothing on `main` at 2026-08-06.

## Ask

Add a step to `.github/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md`:

- Before announcing a release, name one feature that CANNOT exist in the previous version, launch the downloaded artifact, and observe it.
- The step should require naming the feature at cut time (it changes every release), not point at a fixed thing.
- Keep the stamp check too -- this is a second, independent line, not a replacement.

Small. The value is that it makes the identity check a habit rather than a thing someone improvises when suspicious.

Source: #1067 (closing). Family: `docs/POSTMORTEM_2026-07-31_LEAGUE_DAY.md`, #1027.

issues.title: IP / trademark follow-up -- Australian lawyers, DUE Monday 2026-08-03
issues.body:
**Due: Monday 2026-08-03.** Pip solves this when he speaks to Australian lawyers. Explicitly **not urgent before the league launch** -- filed so it cannot be lost in league-night noise.

## Why this exists

Tracked in `beacon-internal#15`. Pip asked to be **forced** on this one. The premortem trigger fired when grant money arrived: the point at which the project has money attached is the point at which unregistered name/mark exposure stops being theoretical.

## The ask on Monday

Bring to the Australian lawyers:

- [ ] Trade mark position for **P(Doom)** / **P(Doom)1** -- searchable? registrable? already conflicted?
- [ ] Which class(es) -- software/games is the obvious one; check whether the education/AI-safety framing needs a second
- [ ] Relationship between the **Beacon** entity and the game IP -- who owns what, and is an assignment needed
- [ ] Whether the public launch + live leaderboard changes the position (prior use, disclosure timing)
- [ ] Cost and timeline for filing

## Context worth handing over

- Public site live at pdoom1.com, public builds shipping since v0.11.0
- First public league night: Fri 2026-07-31
- Manifund application live, deadline 2026-09-09 (website #194) -- funding and IP questions touch each other

## Close condition

Not "asked the lawyers" -- **a written position on whether to file, in which classes, and by when.**
